candidates.summary: Maximum inner product search (MIPS) sits at the core of recommendation systems, search, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). The original data point associated with that best-matching key is then used to handle the query: in RAG, the document that is best suited to answer the question is typically prefixed to the query. candidates.title: GHARP: Real-Time Gaussian Head Animation from Large-Scale Reconstruction Prior
candidates.summary: We present GHARP (Real-time Gaussian Head Animation from Large-scale Reconstruction Prior), a method that animates 3D human heads in real time from a few input images of a subject and a driving expression signal. We decouple the problem into an identity stage that builds a representation of the subject’s geometry and appearance offline, and an animation stage that predicts expression-dependent residuals on top of it at runtime. candidates.title: A question on the code used in AI
candidates.summary:
Why is it using higher level languages like Python, that are very slow to process and not Assembly or C for both size and optimisation.

Using lower levels makes size smaller and usage for CPU, GPU, RAM becomes lower.

For example Hello world in assembly or C takes 5seconds to proces while in python it takes around a min. I tryed to find information but the only thing I found was Higher levels are easier to read.

candidates.summary: Recent work on robot manipulation has focused on specialist policies trained on demonstrations. We show that generalist AI models can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies such as vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world-action models (WAMs). candidates.summary: Can a sender that only computes hashes, with a language model only at the receiver, transmit short human text more cheaply than a classical sender trained on the same domain?
